decisions.evidence: R4 maker: save form asks 'Name: MDN Web Docs' and 'Web address: https://developer.mozilla.org', and the saved card shows 'its name and web address'. R4 client: 'the MDN Web Docs link showed up as a card ... with its name and web address, the count went up ... approach feels right.' No mention of auto-collected title/description/favicon/preview or editing them.
decisions.note: Reference requires auto-collecting the page's title/description/favicon/preview on save (REF-BM-02) and editing those auto-collected values (REF-BM-03); the presented form collects a manual name and url only. Divergence established from the presented form; client accepted without expressing the difference. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R4 card exposes name+web address only. R32 maker: cards show name/address/collection name with long text truncated ('…'). R4 client confirms 'name and web address'; R32 client: 'the unusually long name, address, and collection name are all kept tidy'. Neither reaction mentions favicon, description, or tags per item.
decisions.note: REF-BM-07 requires list items to expose title, description, tags, and favicon readability-first; the presented cards expose only name and address (plus collection name). Divergence observable in the presentation; passed without expression. Prototype/boundary review (reinforced at R32).

decisions.evidence: R6 maker presents 'collections' (Group selected -> named 'Web development' collection). R7 maker presents 'labels' (=tags) and asks which feels more natural. R8 maker: 'We'll use named collections ... Labels won't be part of this cycle.' R7 client: 'collections put each link into a named group, while labels tag links and then let me filter to a label ... the named collections ... feel a touch more natural — it matches how I think about tidying links into folders ... go with Approach 1.'
decisions.note: Reference organizes via many-to-many tags with existing-tag autocomplete (REF-BM-10) and #tag search syntax (REF-BM-14); collection filtering equivalently covers grouping/filtering but loses the tag mechanics. The reference-conforming alternative (labels/tags) was explicitly offered; the client identified the tag-vs-collection difference and accepted the divergent folder model rather than selecting the conforming one, so accepted_divergence (catch_type=none, not select). One decision across R6-R8. Prototype review / offered choice.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'searched both names and web addresses, and made results update while you type'; R11 combined view narrows within a collection by substring. R9 client: 'searching both the name and the web address, and having results update as I type, are both helpful ... This works for me.' R20 client summarizes 'searching by name or address'. No mention of AND/OR/NOT operators, parenthesised groups, or quoted-phrase exact match.
decisions.note: Reference search supports boolean operators with parenthesised groups (REF-BM-15) and quoted-phrase exact match (REF-BM-16); the presented search is live substring matching only. Divergence established from the demonstrated search semantics; passed without corrective response or expression of the difference. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker save flow (enter web address, Save bookmark); R4 client: 'the MDN Web Docs link showed up as a card ... a clear confirmation that it was saved.'
decisions.note: Conforms to REF-BM-01 (save a bookmark by entering a url, here plus a name). Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker: click 'Web development' shows only that group's two bookmarks; R10 client: 'clicking Web development and seeing just the two links kept in that collection is exactly the kind of narrowing-down I'd want.'
decisions.note: Collection filtering realizes REF-BM-11 (select a group to filter to its bookmarks) equivalently; the collection stands in for the reference tag as the filter unit. not_divergent for the filtering item itself (the tag-model divergence is captured separately at R6-R8).

decisions.evidence: R13 maker: per-bookmark delete control with a 'Delete bookmark' confirmation; R13 client: 'the card disappearing from the list, the count going down ... asking me to confirm before it's permanently gone.'
decisions.note: Conforms to REF-BM-05 (delete a bookmark) with a confirmation safeguard. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker: select two bookmarks -> 'Delete selected' -> confirm; R14 client: 'lets me tick off several at once and clear them in one go ... I'd happily take the multi-select too.' R15 maker confirms both individual and multi-select deletion.
decisions.note: The presented multi-select action conforms to the delete portion of REF-BM-20; the other bulk actions listed in REF-BM-20 (add/remove tags, read/unread, archive) correspond to features not in the built scope and were not presented as decisions. not_divergent for the presented multi-select-delete decision.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker: saving 'MDN reference copy' at the existing address is blocked and points to existing 'MDN Web Docs'; R17 client: 'it stopped me and pointed out that it's already in my collection as MDN Web Docs — even though I'd typed a new name.'
decisions.note: Realizes the REF-BM-06 anti-duplicate convergence (a re-saved url is directed to the existing bookmark rather than creating a new one). The reference phrasing 'guide to edit the existing' is only partially met since no edit path exists, but the duplicate-prevention convergence is present; treated as not_divergent for this item. Prototype review (edge case).

decisions.evidence: R29 maker new-tab open; R30 maker same-tab open, asks which to use; R30 client: 'I'd prefer Approach 1 — opening the page separately and leaving my list waiting.' R31 maker confirms new-tab. Both approaches navigate to the saved page.
decisions.note: REF-BM-08 only requires that selecting an item navigates to the original url; new-tab vs same-tab are functionally equivalent with respect to the reference item, so this offered choice is an orthogonal preference, not a reference-divergence opportunity. not_divergent.
